top.title: Microsoft mega outage: Report reveals testing gaps and emails that never arrived
top.description: Some emails never reached their recipients during November's Microsoft 365 outage, the company has confirmed in a final report that also exposes gaps in its testing and recovery procedures. The post-incident report details how a Windows defect brought down Exchange Online and disrupted features across other Microsoft 365 services. For affected users, the cloud became someone else's unavailable computer. A preliminary report had already blamed a July code change, combined with a failover and reduced capacity. The final report confirms those findings and sets out Microsoft's plans to improve change auditing and recovery procedures, and add spare capacity. The defect affected Microsoft's gateway server configuration, not standard Windows deployments. The epic outage (named the "Microsoft long weekend" by some wags) kicked off on November 12 and wasn't fully resolved until November 14. Microsoft extended its delivery retry window to 48 hours, but some delayed messages destined for consumer mailboxes inactive for more than 30 days still expired, generating non-delivery reports. The company said all queued enterprise messages were eventually delivered, with none found permanently lost. The report is grim, particularly in how the failure ramped up as US users came online to find gateway servers toppling over. At the worst point, more than 80 percent of North American gateway servers were unresponsive. The problem proved elusive, and it took Microsoft some time to identify the change and deploy a fix. Microsoft has had a week to ponder what it did and did not do, and the report has some next steps to avoid a repeat of November's events. Some are obvious, and some are a little surprising. Working to reduce the blast radius of failures is an obvious one, and actions include partitioning and isolation to ensure failures can be contained before taking down traffic globally. Recovery procedures also need improvement, along with communication and capacity to ensure there is sufficient headroom. Microsoft's load tests used older, lower-core-count hardware, making them less likely to expose a defect that worsened on newer machines. The company now plans to test newer hardware with more realistic traffic and peak loads, and broaden its failover testing. Microsoft also plans to improve diagnostics and change auditing so engineers can identify troublesome Windows changes faster. July's defect had been running worldwide for more than three months before it brought the gateways down. ®

top.title: PFF Grades Reveal Detroit Lions’ Biggest Standouts From Win Over Buccaneers
top.description: The Detroit Lions beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 31-21 on Sunday , and the Detroit Lions PFF grades include a linebacker who needed only 25 snaps to make the list. Detroit improved to 8-2 on the season with the win, while Tampa Bay dropped to 3-7. Here are the top three Lions on each side of the ball, according to PFF . Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) tucks the ball and runs for the first down while being chased by Tampa Bay Buccaneers outside linebacker Al-Quadin Muhammad (97) during the second half of the NFL game at Ford Field in Detroit, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Chuck Clark led the defense in Detroit Lions PFF grades Safety Chuck Clark led Detroit’s defense on PFF with a grade of 85.7. He played 69 snaps in the game. Clark had eight combined tackles (two solo), one sack, one TFL, and one pass deflection. He had another solid game for the Lions on defense. Linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez was ranked second on the Lions defense on PFF for this matchup against Tampa Bay. He played 55 snaps and had an 83.5 grade on PFF . Rodriguez had six tackles, 0.5 sacks, and one pass deflection. Linebacker K.J. Britt was ranked fifth overall in the game, and he was Detroit’s third-best defensive player. He had a 75.1 PFF grade and played just 25 snaps. Britt had three tackles and one TFL in the game. Jared Goff led the Lions offense on PFF Quarterback Jared Goff had a strong day for the Lions. He completed 20 of 28 passes for 279 yards and two touchdowns without an interception. Goff had the highest grade on offense for the team on PFF . He played 58 snaps and had a grade of 88.3. Jahmyr Gibbs and Jameson Williams round out the top three Running back Jahmyr Gibbs was ranked second on PFF for the Lions on offense. He had an 82.7 grade and played 43 snaps. Gibbs rushed for 98 yards and two touchdowns on 23 carries. He also had four receptions for 20 yards. Gibbs continues to be a workhorse for the Lions on offense. Wide receiver Jameson Williams was the third-best Lions offensive player on PFF, but he was ranked fourth overall in the game. Williams played 45 snaps and had a 74.5 PFF grade . He caught four passes for 93 yards, an average of 23.3 yards per reception, including a 57-yard touchdown. The Bears are next on Thanksgiving This was another huge game for the offense and defense. The Lions will need this kind of performance again in a Thanksgiving showdown with first place on the line against the Chicago Bears, who are also 8-2.

top.title: TELEGRAPH: Williams-Barnett on the brink of a new Tottenham contract
top.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 21: Luca Williams-Barnett of Tottenham Hotspur is the centre of attention as his colleagues celebrate his opening goal during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Tottenham Hotspur and Ipswich Town at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on November 21, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Mark Leech/Offside/Offside via Getty Images) | Offside via Getty Images Well, THAT didn’t take long! Two days after Luca Williams-Barnett introduced himself to the Premier League with a great flourish — scoring a goal and tallying an assist in his first ever Premier League start and leading Spurs to a 2-0 win over Ipswich Town — he’s on the verge of signing a lucrative new contract that will keep him at Tottenham Hotspur for the foreseeable future. According to Matt Law in the Telegraph , Williams-Barnett is very close to signing a new deal with Spurs that will lock down his future at the club. Williams-Barnett is one of the brightest young stars to come out of any Premier League academy in recent years, and the list of clubs that are interested in trying to buy him away from Spurs is long, but includes Chelsea and Borussia Dortmund. It’s also a very unique opportunity for Luca, who due to injuries to Savio, Wilson Odobert, and Mykhailo Mudryk, now has a claim to the starting left winger role at Spurs. Williams-Barnett is only 18 years old, but has made a significant splash in the league, probably as big a splash as any Tottenham academy grad since before Harry Kane. Interestingly, while left back appears to be his current position, Law cites people close to Spurs who suggest LWB could end up being an attacking midfield #10 in the future, and that’s likely his best position. The left wing position is crowded at Spurs (though injury certainly has opened a window for Luca), as is the #10 role, with James Maddison and Xavi Simons, as well as players like Mateus Fernandes, Omar Marmoush, and Conor Gallagher able to play there. But you can certainly make an argument that Maddison is unlikely to be around for too much longer as he ages, and LWB could easily rotate into the position alongside Simons and whoever else Spurs decide to bring in for the future. It’s an exciting time to be a Spurs fan, that’s for sure. Hopefully we’ll see Luca lining up for Tottenham for years to come.

top.description: FIFA announced Monday that the USA will co-host the 2031 Women's World Cup with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, while the UK will host in 2035 (OZAN KOSE) FIFA on Monday confirmed that a joint bid led by the United States will host the expanded, 48-team Women's World Cup in 2031, while the United Kingdom will host the following edition in 2035. The winning bids were waved through by acclamation after FIFA president Gianni Infantino confirmed the USA in partnership with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica was the "sole candidacy" to host in 2031, when the tournament will feature 48 teams for the first time. The joint English, Scottish, Northern Irish and Welsh bid was also the only candidacy for 2035. Infantino had already revealed last year that the respective bids for 2031 and 2035 were unchallenged and therefore set to be awarded the tournaments, with both being officially rubber-stamped at a virtual gathering of FIFA's member associations. "As of 2031 there will be 48 teams and four hosts," said Infantino. "This is an incredible growth in just a few years." The next Women's World Cup will take place next year in Brazil, running from June 24 to July 25. It will feature 32 teams, with the final at the Maracana Stadium in Rio de Janeiro. Spain go into that tournament as the holders after winning the last Women's World Cup held in Australia and New Zealand in 2023, when they defeated current European champions England in the final. The US co-hosted this year's men's World Cup, with the majority of matches being played on American soil, including the final at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey which was won by Spain. That was the first men's edition featuring 48 teams. The United States are the reigning Olympic women's football champions. No senior men's or women's World Cup has been played in the UK since England hosted and won the men's edition in 1966. A joint statement by the four UK national associations described the announcement as "a landmark moment". It is not yet known which cities will host matches at the respective tournaments, but most matches in 2031 are likely to take place in the United States while England can expect to have the lion's share of venues in 2035. top.title: Bucks to continue to push league for NBA All-Star game in Milwaukee
top.description: Despite losing the 2028 NBA All-Star Game to Miami, the Milwaukee Bucks will continue pushing NBA officials for the event. The club believes Milwaukee has everything the NBA needs to host such an event. “We’re going to constantly bring it up with the league,” said Bucks president Josh Glessing. “The opportunity to showcase Milwaukee via the All-Star Game is so important. The economic impact and activity it creates in a region is so powerful." Glessing admits the pitch for Milwaukee does have some "challenges." “What we know is there’s a minimum threshold of hotel rooms and we have work to do there,” Glessing said adding the team has helped build two new hotels in The Trade and AC Hotel by Marriot which is currently under construction. The NBA requires the host city of the All-Star Game to have 7,250 hotel rooms. According to Visit Milwaukee there are 190 hotel properties in the area equaling about 20,000 rooms. It's unclear how many four and five-star hotels are required for the host city. Visit Milwaukee has not talked to the NBA about Milwaukee hosting the all-star game but is supportive of a bid. More: Milwaukee Bucks approach new challenge: getting fans engaged, in seats Glessing is not a stranger to All-Star Games. When he was interim-president of business operations for the Columbus Crew, the organization hosted the MLS All-Star Game in 2024. Glessing said for the team, the All-Star Game is a "money loser" but an event like that has broader economic potential for a city. “It’s a tremendous amount of work and the local teams put so much effort into it, but for the teams it is not a boon in any stretch,” Glessing said. “But for the local economy its so powerful, it’s so impactful to all of the people and activity and dollars that are spent locally. It’s not just a one-day event, it’s a weeklong event. So, the ability to highlight the city is huge.” This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: Bucks to continue to push league for NBA All-Star game in Milwaukee

top.title: Do Cowboys Fans Have Playoff Hope During Thanksgiving Week?
top.description: turkey dak jerry Somebody once said, “Hope is not a plan.” But what if “hope” is just about all you have left to cling to? The Dallas Cowboys crushed the lowly Tennessee Titans, 51-30, Sunday at AT&T Stadium and in doing so fueled optimism inside the locker room. “It gives me hope that we can do some of the things that we want to do,” said owner Jerry Jones (who was technically standing outside the locker room, but you get the point). “We want to get better defensively, and we want to execute like that offensively. “That thing went exactly like it was mapped out to go.” That rings true. Dak Prescott had a historic day, going 28-of-33 for 325 yards and four TDs, while the offense scored TDs on its first six possessions. And on defense? Oh, they gave up yards and they gave up points, but Quinnen Williams led the charge on a five-sack day, capping a week in which young defensive coordinator Christian Parker was demoted , with Mike Pettine now the play-caller. But later in the day came the problem. The Cowboys may have “mapped out” a win, and they can do the same thing as it regards a pursuit of the NFC East title and a playoff berth. But once Jerry and the ’Boys got home to do some scoreboard-watching? They discovered that the Giants pulled off a 23-18 upset over the Jacksonville Jaguars, moving New York to 6-3-1 … meaning that even though Dallas is 5-6, no ground was actually gained. Can Cowboys Nation allow itself to get excited about topping the one-win Titans? Hey, Dallas has lost home games to the Bucs and the Cardinals, so you take the win. Can Dallas fans count on a Thanksgiving win over the visiting (and semi-tanking) Philadelphia Eagles on Thursday? Hey, Dallas is an 8.5-point favorite , so that’s a start. But in the end, does it add up to playoff “hope” for Dallas? Cowboys Nation, you will have to make up your own mind on that one.

nigeria.title: NSCIA to politicians: Keep 2027 campaign violence out of mosques
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA) has condemned attacks in and around some mosques, warning politicians and other actors against using places of worship as grounds for violence and confrontation ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Council said no political disagreement, doctrinal differences or personal grievances could justify violence against worshippers, insisting that mosques must remain sanctuaries of worship and peace, not arenas for settling disputes. The warning was contained in a statement by the NSCIA Secretary-General, Prof. Ishaq Oloyede, on behalf of the Council, led by its President-General, the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar. Describing the attacks as reprehensible and fundamentally contrary to Islamic teachings, the Council stressed that every Muslim had a duty to respect the sanctity of mosques and protect the lives and dignity of worshippers. “These teachings leave no room for violence, intimidation, harassment, assault, attack on or threat against people’s safety and lives in the name of doctrinal differences, political disagreement, socio-economic grievance or any other cause,” it said. The NSCIA maintained that all Muslims had equal rights in mosques and that no worshipper should be intimidated, harassed or attacked under any guise within or around mosque premises. In a specific demand for action against those responsible, the Council urged mosque authorities to assist in identifying perpetrators and provide video recordings of the incidents to law enforcement agencies to facilitate their arrest. It also urged Muslims with grievances to seek redress through dialogue, constructive advocacy, lawful engagement and the courts rather than resorting to violence. “No grievance, however genuine or contrived for expediency, should become a justification for violence or the violation of human dignity or the desecration of the Houses of Allah,” the Council declared. Citing the Qur’an’s injunction against aggression, the NSCIA reminded Muslims of the directive to “cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression” (Qur’an 5:2). The Council also cautioned political actors across party lines, religious leaders, community leaders and members of the public against inflammatory statements and actions capable of escalating tensions or threatening public peace. “They should also stop, henceforth, from desecrating the mosques through acts of violence and desist from embarrassing the nation,” it said. Reaffirming its commitment to peace, justice, dialogue and national unity, the NSCIA said it would continue engaging the government, security agencies and other stakeholders to protect religious freedoms and promote national stability. The Council prayed for the recovery of those injured, comfort for affected persons and lasting peace, security and justice in Nigeria. nigeria.title: Simeone sets La Liga record with 345 wins for Atletico Madrid
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Diego Simeone became the manager with the most victories in La Liga history after Atletico Madrid’s 3-0 victory over Getafe on Sunday, taking his tally to 345 wins in the Spanish top flight. Atletico confirmed the milestone in a statement, saying Simeone had moved past club legend Luis Aragonés, who finished his La Liga career with 344 victories. Simeone reached the record in 189 fewer matches than Aragonés. The 56-year-old said he was pleased with the achievement and pointed to the work behind it. “It makes me happy,” Simeone said. “I don’t usually find many things to be happy about, but there is an incredible amount of work behind this.” Atletico said Simeone has won 60 per cent of the league matches he has managed. The Argentine has led the club since December 2011, when Barcelona and Real Madrid were the dominant sides in Spain. Asked about the criticism that his teams are too defensive, Simeone said it was a constant narrative but questioned whether defence alone could account for his record. “This narrative that we’re a defensive team, as if we’re always playing solely to defend. You don’t win 345 matches just by defending. Is that even possible?” he said. Simeone has also won eight trophies with Atletico: two La Liga titles, one Copa del Rey, one Spanish Super Cup, two UEFA Super Cups and two Europa League crowns. The club noted that he has won two more trophies than Aragonés did during his time in charge. His first silverware came in 2012, when Atletico won the Europa League and then the UEFA Super Cup. He guided them to the Copa del Rey in his first full season and their first La Liga title since 1996 the following campaign. Atletico won another league title under him in 2021 and completed a Europa League and UEFA Super Cup double in 2018. Simeone has also taken Atletico to two Champions League finals, losing to city rivals Real Madrid in 2014 and 2016. Atletico have qualified for the Champions League in every full season of his tenure. The record was set as Atletico moved to third in the table after 10 wins from 13 matches. nigeria.title: 4 facilities FIFA President says Nigeria must fix to host FIFA World Cup

nigeria.title: Fury reveals schizophrenia diagnosis ahead of Joshua clash
nigeria.description: Tyson Fury has said he was diagnosed with schizophrenia soon after his world title win over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015. “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in,” said the heavyweight boxer. “It was like a living version of the pits of hell. “I thought I would end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much. “The anxiety was crippling me. I just could not overcome it and that’s when I went and saw the psychiatrist down in London.” Fury has made the revelations about his mental health in a documentary which will be released by Netflix on Friday. The 38-year-old is preparing for the long-awaited all-British heavyweight fight against Anthony Joshua, a fellow former world champion, in Cardiff on December 11 — a bout that will be broadcast live on Netflix. Fury recalled hearing the radio talking to him, and begging wife Paris to get him out of the hospital because “the Illuminati” wanted him. Following his victory over Klitschko, Fury gained weight and struggled with alcohol and drug addiction. “It got that bad I was hearing voices in my mind,” he said. “I wouldn’t be able to sit and have a conversation because I’d be hearing stuff in my mind. “I didn’t know where to turn and no-one knew what to do. I really needed help, or check into rehab or something. I never got a break from it for years. I wanted to be what I thought was normal again.” After Fury was released from hospital, a diagnosis of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder was confirmed. Fury said a turning point in his life came when he was on a night out for Halloween in 2017. “I looked around and could see all the young people and I thought, ‘I had the world in my hands and I threw it all away, and now I’m a fat mess addicted to alcohol’,” he said. But Fury added he channelled his disgust into a comeback which led him to return to training, focus more on his family and claim another world title when he beat Deontay Wilder in 2020. nigeria.title: Why I will never forget Daniel Amokachi – Hull City owner
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Hull City owner Acun Ilıcalı has revealed how his close friendship with former Nigerian international Daniel Amokachi began during the striker’s spell at Turkish club Besiktas, describing their relationship as one that made them “brothers”. Ilıcalı, who was a football reporter covering Besiktas at the time, recalled how he became so close to the club’s players that the coach would sometimes approach him to find out their whereabouts. While speaking on The Overlap Podcast, the Turkish businessman singled out Amokachi as one of the players he shared a particularly close relationship with, adding that the Nigerian trusted him more than other journalists. “One memory from that time I will never forget is Daniel Amokachi. He had played for Everton, so we became brothers with him. Amokachi spoke only to me and nobody else. All the reporters were asking me to let Amokachi speak to them,” Ilıcalı said. He also recalled how much the former Super Eagles striker trusted him, revealing that Amokachi would leave his Mercedes-Benz 500 SL with him whenever he travelled to Nigeria. “He trusted me so much that he would leave his 500 SL when he went to Nigeria. I would drive it to work, and the whole company was shocked. Everyone would ask what it was, and I would say it was my friend’s car,” he added. Ilıcalı also narrated how he once helped Amokachi reach Istanbul in time for a crucial Besiktas fixture against Fenerbahce, despite supporting the latter club. According to him, Amokachi was missing in the days leading up to the derby, leaving the Besiktas coach repeatedly asking about the striker’s whereabouts. On the morning of the match, Amokachi eventually contacted Ilıcalı and disclosed that he had missed his flight and was stranded in London. The Hull City owner admitted that he initially hesitated to inform Besiktas officials because he knew the Nigerian forward could pose a serious threat to his boyhood club. “I asked Daniel where he was, and he said he had missed the flight. I switched the phone off. If I had told the Besiktas directors, they would have brought him by private jet. But Besiktas were playing Fenerbahce, and I am a Fenerbahce fan,” he recalled. However, after considering his position, Ilıcalı decided to inform a Besiktas director, who arranged a private jet to bring Amokachi to Istanbul. The striker arrived at the airport about an hour before the match and was at the stadium roughly 30 to 40 minutes before kick-off. Despite the late arrival, Amokachi made an immediate impact, scoring in the 20th minute of the game. Amokachi joined Besiktas from Everton and made a significant impression during his time in Turkey, recording 25 goals and 23 assists in 112 appearances across all competitions. nigeria.title: Democrats fire starting gun on 2028 White House race
nigeria.description: Democrats fired the starting gun Monday on the race to win back the White House, announcing plans for 12 debates to pick their standard bearer for 2028 as the party looks to build on its sweeping midterm election victory. The first debate is scheduled for June next year, setting the stage for what could be a crowded contest to select a challenger to the Republicans, who must find a successor to term-limited President Donald Trump. The announcement comes as Democrats celebrate their biggest majority in the House of Representatives since the early 1990s, with their victories this month transforming the balance of power in Washington and raising expectations for the next two years. “Democrats are on offense after our historic victories in the midterms, and the DNC is keeping our foot on the gas as we head into the 2028 cycle,” Democratic National Committee chairman Ken Martin said. The party will hold five debates in 2027 and seven in 2028, the final one scheduled for March of that year. The debates will help voters choose the party’s presidential nominee through a series of state-by-state primary elections and caucuses, in which supporters select the candidate they want to face the Republican nominee in November 2028. Under new rules announced Monday, candidates seeking a place on the debate stage must pledge to denounce spending on their behalf by outside political groups, including those that do not disclose their donors. The requirement is intended to curb the influence of wealthy donors and so-called “dark money” in Democratic nomination contests, a longstanding demand of the party’s progressive wing. With a potentially large field, some debates could be spread across two nights, with a maximum of 20 candidates participating. No major Democrat has formally entered the race, but maneuvering is already underway among politicians seeking to become the party’s standard-bearer. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Cross River Bank Launches Its First Bitcoin-Backed Loans With LendingUSA Cross River Bank has launched its first bitcoin-backed loans, working with consumer lender LendingUSA to let eligible borrowers take out between $10,000 and $250,000 against their BTC without selling it. The program is the first time Cross River has originated bitcoin-secured loans itself, according to The Block. LendingUSA runs the application platform, and every loan is made by Cross River, a New Jersey state-chartered bank, according to LendingUSA . How the loans work Borrowers can choose a loan-to-value ratio of 30%, 50% or 70%, which sets how much cash they receive against the value of the bitcoin they pledge. LendingUSA defines the ratio as the loan balance divided by the value of the collateral, so a 50% loan against $100,000 of bitcoin would be $50,000. Two repayment options are offered: interest-only or no monthly payments. On an interest-only loan, borrowers make smaller monthly payments that roughly cover interest, with the principal and any remaining interest due at the end of the term. On a no-monthly-payment loan, the full balance plus interest is due at the end. LendingUSA says borrowers can repay early without penalties or fees . Applicants go through a soft credit check, and LendingUSA says approval rests on the crypto being pledged rather than a credit score. The company says funding typically arrives within one to three business days after the collateral is verified. Custody and margin risk A qualified third-party custodian holds the bitcoin for the life of the loan. Once the loan is repaid in full, the collateral is released back to the borrower, according to the company. The terms carry the usual risk of borrowing against a volatile asset. LendingUSA says that if the value of the bitcoin falls, the loan-to-value ratio rises, and borrowers may be asked to add collateral or pay down the debt to avoid liquidation. The company says it will try to notify borrowers first but cannot guarantee it during fast price moves. The timing matters. Bitcoin was trading near $61,000 on Monday morning, so a borrower at the 70% tier would have far less room before a collateral call than one at the 30% tier. Lower ratios leave a bigger cushion but unlock less cash per bitcoin pledged. LendingUSA markets the loans for uses such as debt consolidation, home improvements and large purchases. The company says it has served more than 200,000 borrowers across its lending business, and the crypto product is its first expansion into digital asset-backed loans. business.title: Bitcoin Core Patches Node-Stall Bug Found by Block’s AI Scanner
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Core Patches Node-Stall Bug Found by Block’s AI Scanner Bitcoin Core developers have disclosed and patched a medium-severity bug that let an attacker temporarily freeze a node’s processing of blocks and transactions, a flaw first flagged by an AI scanner built by Block’s Spiral. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-117348, is fixed in Bitcoin Core versions 30.5, 31.3 and 32.1. The 30.5 and 31.3 releases shipped Friday alongside the public advisory, while 32.1 has carried the fix since Oct. 27. Affected versions run from 29.0 through 29.5, 30.0 through 30.4 and 31.0 through 31.2. The 29.x series has reached end of life and will not get a fix, so operators on that branch need to move to a newer release. How the Core bug worked Bitcoin Core keeps “orphan” transactions, whose parent transactions it has not yet seen, and asks peers that announce them for the missing pieces. Since version 29.0, the software builds a list of an orphan’s parents and checks each one against its mempool and filters before deciding what to request. A single inv message can carry up to 50,000 entries, and the software did not skip duplicates. An attacker could send a node an orphan with thousands of missing parents, then send messages repeating that transaction’s ID 50,000 times. “Each such message stalls the node for over a dozen seconds, during which it processes no messages from other peers, including blocks,” the advisory said. Sending more messages could stretch the disruption out. The fix makes the node process each transaction announced in an inv message only once. The advisory describes a temporary denial-of-service problem and does not describe any way to steal bitcoin or permanently damage a node. It also does not say whether the bug was ever exploited. For a business running an affected node, the stalls could still matter. An exchange could be slow to credit deposits, and a miner could keep working on an outdated view of the chain while its node is stuck. An AI-found bug under a faster disclosure policy The advisory credits an automated LLM scan run through Elias Rohrer’s Project Loupe at Spiral, Block’s open-source bitcoin development arm. Bitcoin Core developer Gregory Sanders validated the finding and brought it to the project’s security team. Loupe is a free scanner that runs AI agents over open-source bitcoin code and only reports findings backed by a working test case. Bitcoin Core, BDK, LDK, rust-bitcoin, Cashu, Blockstream Jade, bitcoinj and SRI signed up for its first round of scans. Rohrer said on a recent podcast that Spiral started the project around March and began continuous scanning in May, with Bitcoin Core in the first batch. Loupe reported the issue on July 8. A developer known as Stutxo independently reported it on Aug. 4, the same day Sanders opened a pull request with the fix, which was merged two days later. business.title: UK FCA Bars Crypto Exchanges From Market Making on Their Own Venues
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine UK FCA Bars Crypto Exchanges From Market Making on Their Own Venues The U.K. will bar crypto exchange operators from trading against their own capital on the venues they run, while a new Treasury order clears independent market makers to trade on those platforms without a separate dealing permission. The Financial Conduct Authority’s final rules say a firm “must not execute any orders against its proprietary capital” on a qualifying trading platform it operates. The FCA’s guidance spells out the effect: a firm “cannot act as a market maker” on its own platform. The restriction takes effect Oct. 25, 2027. The FCA rule itself is not new. The regulator published it on June 30 in policy statement PS26/11, part of a five-document package that completed its crypto rulebook. What changed last week was the Treasury’s side of the framework. What the FCA rule covers The FCA’s rulebook defines a market maker as a person who holds themselves out on a platform on a continuous basis as willing to buy and sell qualifying cryptoassets against their own capital at prices they set. That is the activity operators will be barred from on their own venues. There is one carve-out. An operator with the appropriate permission may still engage in matched principal trading to execute client orders on its platform, as long as it follows the platform’s non-discretionary rules. The FCA warned that this model does not rule out settlement risk, so firms should take steps to minimize it. The bar applies only to the operator’s own platform. Under the same rules, an operator with the right permission can still trade against its own capital outside the venue it runs. It must make clear to clients which capacity it is acting in, and it must manage conflicts of interest. Treasury clears outside market makers The Treasury made the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Cryptoassets) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2026 on Nov. 18. They add a new Article 9UA to the U.K.’s crypto legislation. The article carves two kinds of activity out of the regulated activity of dealing in qualifying cryptoassets as principal. One is activity carried on “otherwise than for the purpose of providing a service to another person.” The other is activity carried on “as a market maker on a qualifying cryptoasset trading platform.” In practice, a third-party firm quoting prices on a U.K. crypto platform would not need the principal-dealing permission for that activity. The text does not say who the market maker has to be, so the bar on operators comes from the FCA’s rules rather than from the Treasury order. The explanatory note says no impact assessment was prepared because no significant new costs are expected. The FCA’s rules also put new duties on platforms that rely on market makers. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine American Bitcoin (ABTC) Lands $150 Million Bitcoin-Backed Credit Line From FalconX American Bitcoin Corp. (ABTC) has secured a $150 million revolving credit facility from FalconX that is backed by its bitcoin, the miner said Monday, giving it a way to raise cash without selling coins from its reserve. The facility was signed by an American Bitcoin subsidiary and is secured by certain of the company’s bitcoin holdings. American Bitcoin said the money can go toward strategic growth opportunities and general corporate purposes. “This $150 million facility provides American Bitcoin with non-dilutive capital to support our continued operations and growth initiatives,” CEO Mike Ho said in the release. Terms of the FalconX facility The FalconX line is committed up to $150 million, and each draw is subject to bitcoin collateral requirements and other customary conditions. Because it is revolving, the company can draw, repay and redraw funds during the term. Borrowings carry a 5.95% loan fee, plus a commitment fee on any undrawn amount. The initial term is two years, with an optional three-year extension at FalconX’s discretion, subject to customary conditions. The company did not name the size of the commitment fee. The facility has an initial collateral ratio of 143%. At that level, drawing the full $150 million would require about $214.5 million in pledged bitcoin, or roughly 3,500 BTC with bitcoin trading near $61,300 early Monday. American Bitcoin did not say whether it has drawn on the line yet. Its release lists the risks, including the possible liquidation of pledged bitcoin if its value falls below required levels, and requirements to post more collateral or repay borrowings on short notice. “Collateralized lending gives American Bitcoin a way to access liquidity while it continues to grow its Bitcoin reserve and scale its business,” said Oliver Sitt, a sales director at FalconX. The prime broker said the deal shows how it can structure working capital for public companies that do not want to sell their holdings. FalconX provides financing, trading and asset management services to institutional clients. entertainment.title: Solape Fayemi Launches Saina Properties Across Four Markets
entertainment.description: For many people, buying property is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. We are building Saina because we believe there is room for a different kind of real estate experience. One where advice comes before the transaction, where due diligence is not treated as an inconvenience, and where people are encouraged to ask questions, understand their options and make informed decisions,” she said at the launch. That philosophy is reflected in the company’s three core areas of expertise: Advisory & Verification, Sales & Brokerage, and Developments . Rather than focusing solely on connecting buyers to properties, Saina brings together the guidance investors need to assess opportunities, the support required to navigate property transactions, and involvement in real estate development. The company is also building on experience gained before its official launch, having supported more than 25 clients with property opportunities across different markets. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. Fayemi’s position raises a familiar question: people consult doctors for medical concerns and lawyers for legal matters, so why do some investors leave significant property decisions in the hands of relatives simply because they are available or familiar with the location? While trust and family relationships matter, they do not automatically translate into the technical knowledge needed to assess a property, verify its documentation or understand its investment potential. These decisions require proper checks, market understanding and accountability. Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. Themed “ Celebrating the Redefiners: Africa’s AI Generation,” the evening honoured young Africans aged 18 to 35 across 26 categories, including technology and innovation, entrepreneurship, governance, music, film, literature, advocacy, sports and fashion. entertainment.description: One of the best aspects of art is its ability to imitate current events or imagine possibilities. Movies, as a powerful art form, present a sequence of events that allows viewers to see reflections of themselves or envision who they could become. At its core, art exists to entertain, inform and critique society. Through films, music and visual expressions, we are continually reminded of our shared humanity—our joys, flaws and contradictions. One subject that art, particularly film, has explored is masculinity. However, this theme is often addressed subtly and can be easy to overlook, as the movies that dominate global box offices frequently focus on spectacle: fantasy, romance, adventure or others. Conversations about men, their inner lives, vulnerabilities and social roles are often not in the top circle. Nonetheless, some films have attempted to explore what it means to be a man in today’s world. They invite audiences to contemplate important questions such as: What is the role of men in society? entertainment.description: What does it really mean to play to win in business and leadership? Beyond earning a seat at the table, it requires more than competence or professional accomplishments. It requires the confidence to own one’s value, the clarity to communicate one’s contributions and the intentionality to build visibility that translates into meaningful influence. These conversations defined The Executive Woman Summit (TEWS) 2.0 , which brought together hundreds of executive women, corporate professionals, entrepreneurs and emerging leaders at Harbour Point, Victoria Island, Lagos, on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. Convened by Bola Matel-Okoh , a dual-qualified attorney (called to both the New York and Nigerian Bars), Executive Coach, Non-Executive Director at Wema Bank, and CEO of BMO Advisory Services , the second edition of the summit was themed Playing to Win: Elevate Your Vision, Value and Visibility. She also challenged the assumption that excellent work will automatically speak for itself, encouraging women to communicate their contributions with evidence and confidence. “What problem did you solve? sports.description: The Detroit Lions beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 31-21 on Sunday , and the Detroit Lions PFF grades include a linebacker who needed only 25 snaps to make the list. Detroit improved to 8-2 on the season with the win, while Tampa Bay dropped to 3-7. Here are the top three Lions on each side of the ball, according to PFF . Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) tucks the ball and runs for the first down while being chased by Tampa Bay Buccaneers outside linebacker Al-Quadin Muhammad (97) during the second half of the NFL game at Ford Field in Detroit, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Chuck Clark led the defense in Detroit Lions PFF grades Safety Chuck Clark led Detroit’s defense on PFF with a grade of 85.7. He played 69 snaps in the game. Clark had eight combined tackles (two solo), one sack, one TFL, and one pass deflection. He had another solid game for the Lions on defense. Linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez was ranked second on the Lions defense on PFF for this matchup against Tampa Bay. He played 55 snaps and had an 83.5 grade on PFF . Rodriguez had six tackles, 0.5 sacks, and one pass deflection. Linebacker K.J. Britt was ranked fifth overall in the game, and he was Detroit’s third-best defensive player. He had a 75.1 PFF grade and played just 25 snaps. Britt had three tackles and one TFL in the game. Jared Goff led the Lions offense on PFF Quarterback Jared Goff had a strong day for the Lions. He completed 20 of 28 passes for 279 yards and two touchdowns without an interception. Goff had the highest grade on offense for the team on PFF . He played 58 snaps and had a grade of 88.3. Jahmyr Gibbs and Jameson Williams round out the top three Running back Jahmyr Gibbs was ranked second on PFF for the Lions on offense. He had an 82.7 grade and played 43 snaps. Gibbs rushed for 98 yards and two touchdowns on 23 carries. He also had four receptions for 20 yards. Gibbs continues to be a workhorse for the Lions on offense. Wide receiver Jameson Williams was the third-best Lions offensive player on PFF, but he was ranked fourth overall in the game. Williams played 45 snaps and had a 74.5 PFF grade . He caught four passes for 93 yards, an average of 23.3 yards per reception, including a 57-yard touchdown. The Bears are next on Thanksgiving This was another huge game for the offense and defense. The Lions will need this kind of performance again in a Thanksgiving showdown with first place on the line against the Chicago Bears, who are also 8-2.

sports.title: TELEGRAPH: Williams-Barnett on the brink of a new Tottenham contract
sports.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 21: Luca Williams-Barnett of Tottenham Hotspur is the centre of attention as his colleagues celebrate his opening goal during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Tottenham Hotspur and Ipswich Town at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on November 21, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Mark Leech/Offside/Offside via Getty Images) | Offside via Getty Images Well, THAT didn’t take long! Two days after Luca Williams-Barnett introduced himself to the Premier League with a great flourish — scoring a goal and tallying an assist in his first ever Premier League start and leading Spurs to a 2-0 win over Ipswich Town — he’s on the verge of signing a lucrative new contract that will keep him at Tottenham Hotspur for the foreseeable future. According to Matt Law in the Telegraph , Williams-Barnett is very close to signing a new deal with Spurs that will lock down his future at the club. Williams-Barnett is one of the brightest young stars to come out of any Premier League academy in recent years, and the list of clubs that are interested in trying to buy him away from Spurs is long, but includes Chelsea and Borussia Dortmund. It’s also a very unique opportunity for Luca, who due to injuries to Savio, Wilson Odobert, and Mykhailo Mudryk, now has a claim to the starting left winger role at Spurs. Williams-Barnett is only 18 years old, but has made a significant splash in the league, probably as big a splash as any Tottenham academy grad since before Harry Kane. Interestingly, while left back appears to be his current position, Law cites people close to Spurs who suggest LWB could end up being an attacking midfield #10 in the future, and that’s likely his best position. The left wing position is crowded at Spurs (though injury certainly has opened a window for Luca), as is the #10 role, with James Maddison and Xavi Simons, as well as players like Mateus Fernandes, Omar Marmoush, and Conor Gallagher able to play there. But you can certainly make an argument that Maddison is unlikely to be around for too much longer as he ages, and LWB could easily rotate into the position alongside Simons and whoever else Spurs decide to bring in for the future. It’s an exciting time to be a Spurs fan, that’s for sure. Hopefully we’ll see Luca lining up for Tottenham for years to come.

The winning bids were waved through by acclamation after FIFA president Gianni Infantino confirmed the USA in partnership with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica was the "sole candidacy" to host in 2031, when the tournament will feature 48 teams for the first time. The joint English, Scottish, Northern Irish and Welsh bid was also the only candidacy for 2035. Infantino had already revealed last year that the respective bids for 2031 and 2035 were unchallenged and therefore set to be awarded the tournaments, with both being officially rubber-stamped at a virtual gathering of FIFA's member associations. "As of 2031 there will be 48 teams and four hosts," said Infantino. "This is an incredible growth in just a few years." The next Women's World Cup will take place next year in Brazil, running from June 24 to July 25. It will feature 32 teams, with the final at the Maracana Stadium in Rio de Janeiro. Spain go into that tournament as the holders after winning the last Women's World Cup held in Australia and New Zealand in 2023, when they defeated current European champions England in the final. The US co-hosted this year's men's World Cup, with the majority of matches being played on American soil, including the final at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey which was won by Spain. That was the first men's edition featuring 48 teams. The USA has hosted the Women's World Cup twice before, in 1999 and 2003, and is also the most successful nation in the tournament's history, having lifted the trophy four times. - 'Landmark moment' - US Soccer reacted to the announcement by saying the awarding of the 2031 tournament gave the country the chance to "build on the momentum" of this year's World Cup as well as the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The United States are the reigning Olympic women's football champions. No senior men's or women's World Cup has been played in the UK since England hosted and won the men's edition in 1966. A joint statement by the four UK national associations described the announcement as "a landmark moment". sports.title: Bucks to continue to push league for NBA All-Star game in Milwaukee
sports.description: Despite losing the 2028 NBA All-Star Game to Miami, the Milwaukee Bucks will continue pushing NBA officials for the event. The club believes Milwaukee has everything the NBA needs to host such an event. “We’re going to constantly bring it up with the league,” said Bucks president Josh Glessing. “The opportunity to showcase Milwaukee via the All-Star Game is so important. The economic impact and activity it creates in a region is so powerful." Glessing admits the pitch for Milwaukee does have some "challenges." “What we know is there’s a minimum threshold of hotel rooms and we have work to do there,” Glessing said adding the team has helped build two new hotels in The Trade and AC Hotel by Marriot which is currently under construction. The NBA requires the host city of the All-Star Game to have 7,250 hotel rooms. According to Visit Milwaukee there are 190 hotel properties in the area equaling about 20,000 rooms. It's unclear how many four and five-star hotels are required for the host city. Visit Milwaukee has not talked to the NBA about Milwaukee hosting the all-star game but is supportive of a bid. More: Milwaukee Bucks approach new challenge: getting fans engaged, in seats Glessing is not a stranger to All-Star Games. When he was interim-president of business operations for the Columbus Crew, the organization hosted the MLS All-Star Game in 2024. Glessing said for the team, the All-Star Game is a "money loser" but an event like that has broader economic potential for a city. “It’s a tremendous amount of work and the local teams put so much effort into it, but for the teams it is not a boon in any stretch,” Glessing said. “But for the local economy its so powerful, it’s so impactful to all of the people and activity and dollars that are spent locally. It’s not just a one-day event, it’s a weeklong event. So, the ability to highlight the city is huge.” This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: Bucks to continue to push league for NBA All-Star game in Milwaukee

sports.title: Do Cowboys Fans Have Playoff Hope During Thanksgiving Week?
sports.description: turkey dak jerry Somebody once said, “Hope is not a plan.” But what if “hope” is just about all you have left to cling to? The Dallas Cowboys crushed the lowly Tennessee Titans, 51-30, Sunday at AT&T Stadium and in doing so fueled optimism inside the locker room. “It gives me hope that we can do some of the things that we want to do,” said owner Jerry Jones (who was technically standing outside the locker room, but you get the point). “We want to get better defensively, and we want to execute like that offensively. “That thing went exactly like it was mapped out to go.” That rings true. Dak Prescott had a historic day, going 28-of-33 for 325 yards and four TDs, while the offense scored TDs on its first six possessions. And on defense? Oh, they gave up yards and they gave up points, but Quinnen Williams led the charge on a five-sack day, capping a week in which young defensive coordinator Christian Parker was demoted , with Mike Pettine now the play-caller. But later in the day came the problem. The Cowboys may have “mapped out” a win, and they can do the same thing as it regards a pursuit of the NFC East title and a playoff berth. But once Jerry and the ’Boys got home to do some scoreboard-watching? They discovered that the Giants pulled off a 23-18 upset over the Jacksonville Jaguars, moving New York to 6-3-1 … meaning that even though Dallas is 5-6, no ground was actually gained. Can Cowboys Nation allow itself to get excited about topping the one-win Titans? Hey, Dallas has lost home games to the Bucs and the Cardinals, so you take the win. Can Dallas fans count on a Thanksgiving win over the visiting (and semi-tanking) Philadelphia Eagles on Thursday? Hey, Dallas is an 8.5-point favorite , so that’s a start. But in the end, does it add up to playoff “hope” for Dallas? Cowboys Nation, you will have to make up your own mind on that one.

sports.title: Eagles star Joe Milton reveals the secret trick he uses every time just before he throws a deep pass
sports.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles picked up a 19-16 upset win over the Pittsburgh Steelers, and Joe Milton played his part. The 26-year-old quarterback was only signed in October this year, following Jalen Hurts’ injury, and he has now started back-to-back games. Against the Steelers, Milton showed off his passing ability, and he revealed the trick he uses to program his mind not to overthrow. Joe Milton says his daughter’s name before every deep pass Milton played a turnover-free, game-manager role in his second start for the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday. The quarterback seemed to develop a good partnership with DeVonta Smith, targeting him 12 times out of his 21 pass attempts. One of his pass attempts flew over the wide receiver’s head, much to his surprise. “I didn’t think I could get overthrown. And he did it,” Smith said. After the game, Milton was asked how he decides when to go hard and when not to when he’s in the middle. The quarterback revealed that his secret trick involves using his daughter’s name. He said, as per NBCS Philly: “Just showing a little love. In throws like that, I usually say my daughter’s name. It helps me relax. I didn’t that time (overthrown pass to Smith), obviously. “Right before I throw the ball, just get a quick little ‘Maleia’, just so I can relax a little bit. Basically, it kind of tells myself and my mind that I’m throwing the ball to her, so it can’t be as hard. “So, show a little love.” Sunday was the first time Smith and Milton played together for the Philadelphia Eagles, and early signs are definitely positive. The quarterback finished the game with 141 passing yards while completing 11 of his 21 passes, boasting a 73.7 passer rating. He also added seven rushing yards on five carries and took three sacks. Milton hasn’t thrown a touchdown pass for the Eagles yet, but he is in line to start against the Dallas Cowboys next, who are his former team. We’re sure he would love to break his duck then. sports.title: Josh Allen Spots Rookie Jacob Rodriguez And Shows Massive Respect
sports.description: Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images Josh Allen stayed on the field after the Bills beat the Dolphins 26-9 on Sunday just to find rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez. The Bills quarterback hunted down the Miami defender, hugged him, and exchanged quick words before heading to the locker room. This moment stood out because Allen usually leaves right after his postgame chat with the media. The game on Sunday, Nov. 22, was a tough night for Allen statistically, even though his team won big. He threw for 304 yards and a touchdown but also tossed two interceptions. Miami’s defense held him to a quarterback rating under 70 and sacked him three times. Rodriguez was a major part of that pressure, finishing with a team-high 13 tackles and one interception. Allen didn’t just leave it at a quick nod. He waited for the rookie to finish his own media obligations. Most veterans do not wait that long for a rookie from a rival team, especially one who just made their life hard. Phin Phanatic noted that Allen’s search showed real respect for the young player’s performance. The Rookie Who Stole the Show Rodriguez made his mark early in the game. He picked off Allen near the end of the first half. It was the second interception of the season for the rookie. Virginia’s Rodriguez began his collegiate tenure as an offensive role/QB after in 2021 then being selected as an All-American linebacker from Texas Tech – 43rd overall in the 2026 class. That shared background might be why Allen wanted to talk to him so badly. Heavy.com reported that fans on social media praised the gesture immediately. One user called it a “Top 10 football respect moment.” Even some Miami fans admitted they found it hard to hate Allen after seeing this. One fan wrote, “As a Dolphins [fan]… it’s hard not to like Josh Allen. He’s a good guy.” A Rare Quiet Game for Allen While the hug got the headlines, the game itself had a strange stat line for the Bills star. Andrew Siciliano pointed out that Allen did not have a single rushing attempt during the entire game. This was the first time in his nine-year NFL career that he played a full game without trying to run the ball. The Bills chose not to let Allen run on a goal-line sneak. James Cook received the handoff instead, scoring a one-yard touchdown. Allen admitted he was not happy with his own play despite the win. He said, “You got to play your best and tonight I don’t feel like I did.” He also noted that he had two bad decisions, one being a tipped pass. “So, got a lot to clean up,” Allen said in his postgame press conference. He added, “It’s very much a luxury to sit here, be 9-1 and be a little ticked off about how you played.” Now the Bills face a short week. They will host the Kansas City Chiefs on Thursday, Nov. 26. The next game for the Dolphins is Sunday, Nov. 29, against the New York Jets.

technology.title: Microsoft mega outage: Report reveals testing gaps and emails that never arrived
technology.description: Some emails never reached their recipients during November's Microsoft 365 outage, the company has confirmed in a final report that also exposes gaps in its testing and recovery procedures. The post-incident report details how a Windows defect brought down Exchange Online and disrupted features across other Microsoft 365 services. For affected users, the cloud became someone else's unavailable computer. A preliminary report had already blamed a July code change, combined with a failover and reduced capacity. The final report confirms those findings and sets out Microsoft's plans to improve change auditing and recovery procedures, and add spare capacity. The defect affected Microsoft's gateway server configuration, not standard Windows deployments. The epic outage (named the "Microsoft long weekend" by some wags) kicked off on November 12 and wasn't fully resolved until November 14. Microsoft extended its delivery retry window to 48 hours, but some delayed messages destined for consumer mailboxes inactive for more than 30 days still expired, generating non-delivery reports. The company said all queued enterprise messages were eventually delivered, with none found permanently lost. The report is grim, particularly in how the failure ramped up as US users came online to find gateway servers toppling over. At the worst point, more than 80 percent of North American gateway servers were unresponsive. The problem proved elusive, and it took Microsoft some time to identify the change and deploy a fix. Microsoft has had a week to ponder what it did and did not do, and the report has some next steps to avoid a repeat of November's events. Some are obvious, and some are a little surprising. Working to reduce the blast radius of failures is an obvious one, and actions include partitioning and isolation to ensure failures can be contained before taking down traffic globally. Recovery procedures also need improvement, along with communication and capacity to ensure there is sufficient headroom. Microsoft's load tests used older, lower-core-count hardware, making them less likely to expose a defect that worsened on newer machines. The company now plans to test newer hardware with more realistic traffic and peak loads, and broaden its failover testing. Microsoft also plans to improve diagnostics and change auditing so engineers can identify troublesome Windows changes faster. July's defect had been running worldwide for more than three months before it brought the gateways down. ®

technology.title: British retailer Next downplays data breach at tech supplier
technology.description: British retailer Next has become the latest high street name to find itself caught up in a cyberattack, although it insists the data accessed by hackers is "benign" and its customers have nothing to worry about. The clothing and homeware giant told investors on Monday that a third-party supplier had suffered a security breach, allowing an unauthorized party to access information relating to Next. The retailer says its own systems remain untouched and that, so far, there's no evidence that customer personal data has fallen into the wrong hands. "We have been informed that one of our third-party online suppliers has experienced a cyber incident which has resulted in unauthorized access to certain benign data relating to NEXT," the company said in its statement, which it shared with The Register . "We took immediate steps to investigate the nature and scope of the incident with the supplier." The breached supplier provides technology services to Next, and the "benign" information accessed is understood to be low-level data. Sensitive customer details, including addresses, passwords, and banking information, are believed to be unaffected. Next hasn't identified the supplier, explained exactly what the hackers managed to get their hands on, or revealed how much information was accessed, and declined to say when asked by The Register . However, the retailer has seemingly decided that the stolen data won’t be of much use to the criminals responsible. "Our investigations are ongoing; however, current evidence indicates that no customer personal data has been compromised," Next said. "The information affected is limited in nature and, based on our current assessment, cannot be used to facilitate fraud against our customers or NEXT." Next also stressed that its own IT infrastructure had escaped unscathed, saying it was "confident that NEXT’s own systems have not been compromised and that this remains an incident affecting the supplier's environment." Despite repeatedly describing the compromised information as harmless, Next says it is treating the incident "with the utmost seriousness" and is working with the affected supplier, law enforcement, and relevant regulators. science.title: The remains of a long-dead volcano on Mars | Space photo of the day for Nov. 23, 2026
science.description: null An image of Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on the surface of Mars, produced by ESA's Mars Express orbiter. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Researchers have spotted an ancient, "dead" Martian volcano from orbit around the Red Planet. What is it? The European Space Agency's Mars Express spacecraft, which has been orbiting and studying the planet since it arrived in 2003, recently captured incredible new imagery of the volcano Tharsis Tholus. This snapshot was captured by the spacecraft's High Resolution Stereo Camera. Even as old and worn as it is, the Martian volcano stands at around 4.97 miles (8 kilometers) tall which is comparable to some of the highest peaks in the Himalayan mountains. Despite its impressive height, it's still only about a medium-sized volcano for Mars, which is home much more impressively-sized volcanoes. For example, the planet's largest volcano Olympus Mons measures in at roughly 13.2 miles high (21.3 kilometers). Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on the surface of Mars, as seen by ESA's Mars Express orbiter. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Why is it incredible? While Tharsis Tholus might not be the tallest volcano on Mars, it is incredibly steep. It is steeper than Mauna Kea in Hawaii on Earth. To fully showcase the volcano's structure and topography in 3D, researchers actually exaggerated the vertical scale in this image, ESA reported . In addition to being steep and fairly tall, the volcano also has an interesting history. You can see that it is speckled with what look like small holes which are actually craters created by impacts from objects like asteroids. The volcano's current, unique shape is a combined effort by these impacts, environmental factors causing erosion and warping and ancient lava flows that left behind built-up material. The observations by Mars Express also reveals cracks and other imperfections in the volcano. All of these details might seem like superficial bits of detail, however every small crater, every lumpy cliffside and every worn down surface hides information about the planet's past. By studying features like volcanoes on Mars, researchers can piece together what the planet may have looked like in its ancient past. How active was this volcano? How did it interact with the landscape around it? Observations like this can hold the answers.

After a tortuous fortnight of negotiations, COP31 ended in disarray late on 22 November after countries including the UK and the EU refused to agree to a political accord that failed to mention fossil fuels. Read more Can everyone live a ‘good life’ without destroying the planet? The Antalya pact would have seen countries officially recognise that the world is on course to exceed 1.5°C degrees of warming and promise to limit the scale of the overshoot as far as possible. It also would have committed nations to increasing the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 per cent globally by 2035, a key target for climate campaigners who see electrification as the route away from fossil-fuel dependency. Advertisement But the draft agreement proved unacceptable to many countries, including the UK, the EU and some small island nations, after all mentions of fossil fuels were omitted at the behest of fossil fuel-dependent nations such as Saudi Arabia and Russia. Failing to mention fossil fuels explicitly in the text would have marked a backwards step for the climate process, the EU argued. At COP28 in Dubai three years ago, nations agreed to “transition away from fossil fuels” , but since then, attempts to strengthen the language or clarify how this transition will take place have been blocked by petrostates. Alden Meyer at the climate think tank E3G says the talks were subjected to a “brutish” strategy from fossil fuel-exporting states to “systematically block” any reference to the COP28 deal. “They clearly have buyer’s remorse about that agreement. science.description: I didn’t expect much as I unboxed the Brainstorm Night Sky; after all, I’m significantly older than this educational star projector’s target audience. Perhaps I’d come away with a sense of wonder and delight, coupled with mild irritation at having to hunt down three AA batteries to power it. Instead, I was filled with envy as the Brainstorm Night Sky reminded me just what I was missing, thanks to the rigors of light pollution . A few minutes after powering it down, I was already making plans for my first dark sky trip, yearning for a view that rivaled the Brainstorm’s cosmic images. Brainstorm Night Sky Projector review Whatever your age, the Brainstorm Night Sky is so simple to use The Brainstorm Night Sky projector comes with four or six slides, depending on whether you buy the blue or gray version (Image credit: Chris McMullen) Draw the curtains, press the Night Sky’s single button (tilting the projector and twisting the focus as appropriate) and it projects a circular image onto a ceiling or wall. Press the button again and the projection slowly begins to rotate, slowly but stutter-free. It really is that simple to operate and, aimed at budding astronomers aged eight or above, it's reasonably lightweight without feeling flimsy. Depending on the model you buy, you’ll get four or six interchangeable slides. (Image credit: Chris McMullen) Specifications Weight: 14.8 oz (420 g) Bulb type: Non-specified Laser: No Control: On-unit Rotation: Yes, one speed Projection area: Up to 8.2 ft (2.5 m) Sleep timer: Yes (30 mins) Power: 3x AA batteries Speaker: No I was initially a little surprised by the size of the projection: at up to 8.2 feet (2.5 m) wide it’s not going to fill an entire ceiling. It also switches off after 30 minutes, a limit that can’t be disabled, so if you’re looking to put on your own space-themed party this is not the projector for you. But it’s on point for home education and, priced from $49.99, the Brainstorm Night Sky projector won’t break the bank. The spacecraft's mission included the study of Mars and the Martian moon Phobos, with a planned close approach and deployment of landing probes, and over the next several months, the spacecraft successfully captured more than three dozen images of Phobos during its time in service. However, early in the following year, the spacecraft's mission abruptly ended after the Phobos 2 ground team mysteriously lost contact with the spacecraft. Adding to the mystery were objects in some of the final photographs dispatched by the doomed spacecraft, which seemed to show an elongated shadow beneath the probe — a strange twist in one of the Soviet Union's final space missions, and one that soon gave rise to conspiracy theories about what the fate of Phobos 2 might have been. So what caused the odd-looking appearance of the shadow in the final images captured by Phobos 2, and what was the real reason behind the spacecraft's sudden failure?
